newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-ALBORETO TAKES POLE WITH RECORD PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ALBORETO TAKES POLE WITH RECORD PERFORMANCE.

text.p: Ex-Formula One driver Michele Alboreto smashed the circuit qualifying record by five seconds on Thursday as he booked pole position for the Le Mans 24-hour race this weekend.
The Italian took last year's winning car -- a Porsche-powered open sports prototype built by Britain's Tom Walkinshaw -- around the 13.6 km French circuit in three minutes 41.581 seconds.
Alboreto was 2.6 seconds quicker than the second-fastest factory Porsche GT of Belgian Thierry Boutsen, who failed to improve on Wednesday's qualifying time.
Third best was Finland's J.J. Lehto, winner of this year's three world GT championship rounds in a BMW McLaren.
Final qualifying was halted twice. First a 1.6 km oil slick was laid by one of the cars, then Italiasn Gianni Lavaggi escaped unhurt after crashing heavily in a Kremer-Porsche prototype.
In another incident, Briton Chris Goodwin had to leap out of his Gulf McLaren when it burst into flames after an oil line fractured.
